title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第46部分：日志、流与数据仓库

chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

f3d86d1945ef.en: A log, in the sense of this part, is the simplest data structure that remembers time: records appended one after another, each with a number, its offset, and never changed. <bookmark mark='a'/> We have met it again and again. A database writes every change to a log before it touches the data. Raft agrees on a log, and every replica applies it in order. Git's history is a log of snapshots. The outbox of Part 43 is a log of events. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2013 Jay Kreps, who had built LinkedIn's data infrastructure, argued that the log is the unifying abstraction of real-time data: the right way to move data between all of a company's systems.
f3d86d1945ef.zh: 本部分所说的日志，是能记住时间的最简单的数据结构：记录一条接一条地追加，每条带一个编号，即它的偏移量（offset），而且永不改动。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们已经一次又一次地遇到它。数据库在动数据之前，先把每一次变更写进日志。Raft 就一份日志达成一致，每个副本按顺序应用它。Git 的历史是一份快照的日志。第43部分的发件箱（outbox）是一份事件的日志。<bookmark mark='b'/>2013年，曾搭建 LinkedIn 数据基础设施的 Jay Kreps 提出，日志是实时数据的统一抽象：是在一家公司所有系统之间搬运数据的正确方式。

9c29c42e3b25.en: Here is the argument. <bookmark mark='a'/> A company has sources of data, databases and streams of clicks, and systems that need them: a search index, a cache, a warehouse, a fraud model. Connect each source to each consumer directly and you build sixteen pipelines, each with its own format and its own failures. <bookmark mark='b'/> Put a log in the middle instead. Every source appends to it, and every consumer reads from it: eight connections. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each consumer keeps its own position, reads at its own pace, and can go back and replay history. A new consumer starts at the beginning and catches up.
9c29c42e3b25.zh: 论证是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>一家公司有数据源，比如数据库和点击流；也有需要这些数据的系统：搜索索引、缓存、数据仓库、反欺诈模型。把每个数据源直接连到每个消费者，你就要建16条管道，每条都有自己的格式、自己的故障。<bookmark mark='b'/>换个做法，在中间放一份日志。每个数据源都往里追加，每个消费者都从中读取：只要8条连接。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个消费者保存自己的位置，按自己的节奏读，还能回头重放历史。新的消费者从头开始，逐步追上。

2f71b2239742.en: So every company's data ends up in two places. <bookmark mark='a'/> An append-only log, recording everything as it happens. <bookmark mark='b'/> A column-oriented warehouse, laid out to answer questions about all of it at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> And between them, stream processors that compute answers continuously, as the data flows. <bookmark mark='d'/> The hard part, we will see, is time: events arrive late, out of order, and more than once, and a correct answer has to survive all three.
2f71b2239742.zh: 所以，每家公司的数据最终都落在两个地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>一份只追加的日志，记录发生的一切。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个面向列的数据仓库，它的布局是为了一次性回答关于全部数据的问题。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在两者之间，是流处理器，随着数据流动持续地计算答案。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们会看到，难点在于时间：事件会迟到、会乱序、会重复到达，而正确的答案必须经受住这三者。

955e43148952.en: This is Part 46 of Computer Science, Built. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will build a partitioned log with consumer groups; turn a database's changes into a stream; give windows of events a notion of time that survives lateness; checkpoint a running computation so that it recovers with exactly-once state; take apart a columnar file down to its encodings and the levels that let nested data live in columns; and end with the Job as a live top twenty over a stream of novels.
955e43148952.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第46部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会构建一个带消费者组的分区日志；把数据库的变更变成一条流；给事件窗口一种能经受迟到的时间概念；为运行中的计算做检查点，让它恢复时具有恰好一次的状态；把一个列式文件拆开，一直拆到它的编码，以及让嵌套数据能存进列里的那些级别；最后把那项任务做成一条小说流上实时更新的前20名。

accae8c27c70.en: Kafka was built at LinkedIn by Jay Kreps, Neha Narkhede and Jun Rao, and described in 2011. <bookmark mark='a'/> A topic, a named stream such as page views, is split into partitions, and each partition is a log: records appended at the end, numbered by offset, and never changed. <bookmark mark='b'/> On disk a partition is a run of segment files, each named by its first offset, with a sparse index into it. Only the last segment is written; by default a new one starts every gigabyte. <bookmark mark='c'/> A consumer's whole state is one number per partition, the next offset to read, which it commits back to the broker and resumes from after a crash.
accae8c27c70.zh: Kafka 由 Jay Kreps、Neha Narkhede 和 Jun Rao 在 LinkedIn 构建，并于2011年发表。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个主题（topic），也就是一条有名字的流，比如页面浏览，被分成若干分区，每个分区都是一份日志：记录追加在末尾，按偏移量编号，永不改动。<bookmark mark='b'/>在磁盘上，一个分区是一串段文件，每个以它的第一个偏移量命名，并带有一个指向其中的稀疏索引。只有最后一个段会被写入；默认每满1吉字节就开始一个新段。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个消费者的全部状态，就是每个分区一个数字：下一个要读的偏移量。它把这个数字提交回 broker，崩溃之后就从那里接着读。

89c5a844ccca.en: Which partition does a record go to? <bookmark mark='a'/> The producer hashes the record's key. Here the keys are words, hashed with CRC thirty-two into four partitions. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every record with the same key lands in the same partition, so one key's records keep their order, and our simulator checks this for every key. Order per key is Kafka's guarantee, and usually what an application needs: all the changes to one customer, in order. <bookmark mark='c'/> Across partitions there is no order at all. And hot keys make hot partitions: the common words fill two partitions, while another holds a single ship.
89c5a844ccca.zh: 一条记录该进哪个分区？<bookmark mark='a'/>生产者对记录的键做哈希。这里的键是单词，用 CRC32 哈希到4个分区里。<bookmark mark='b'/>键相同的记录总落在同一个分区，所以同一个键的记录保持顺序，我们的模拟器对每个键都检查了这一点。按键有序是 Kafka 的保证，通常也正是应用所需要的：同一位客户的所有变更，按顺序排好。<bookmark mark='c'/>跨分区则完全没有顺序。而热键造成热分区：常见词塞满了两个分区，另一个分区却只装着一条 ship。

34a8fdf297fa.en: Readers share the work through a consumer group. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each partition is read by exactly one member, so a group can grow to as many members as there are partitions, and another group reads the same log independently. Here three members hold four partitions each. <bookmark mark='b'/> A fourth member joins, and the group rebalances. Range assignment recuts four contiguous runs and moves six partitions. A sticky assignor moves only three, the fewest possible, since the newcomer needs three. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then member two leaves: range moves four partitions, sticky just the three that member two owned. Each moved partition pauses while its new owner resumes from the committed offset.
34a8fdf297fa.zh: 读者通过消费者组来分担工作。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个分区恰好由一个成员读取，所以一个组最多可以扩展到和分区数一样多的成员，而另一个组可以独立地读同一份日志。这里3个成员各持有4个分区。<bookmark mark='b'/>第4个成员加入，组进行再均衡。范围分配重新切出4段连续的分区，移动了6个分区。粘性分配器只移动3个，这是可能的最少数目，因为新成员需要3个。<bookmark mark='c'/>接着2号成员离开：范围分配移动4个分区，粘性分配器只移动2号成员原有的那3个。每个被移动的分区都会暂停，直到新的所有者从已提交的偏移量处接着读。

25c88a3e622a.en: A log cannot grow for ever, and there are two ways to forget. <bookmark mark='a'/> By time: whole segments older than the retention period, seven days by default, are deleted, and the start offset moves forward. Deleting a file is cheap, which is one reason segments exist. <bookmark mark='b'/> By key: a compacted topic keeps only the latest record for each key, at its original offset, and a record with an empty value, a tombstone, deletes its key. <bookmark mark='c'/> What remains is the latest state, and it is enough: in our simulator, two thousand updates to fifty keys compact to fifty records, which rebuild exactly the same table.
25c88a3e622a.zh: 日志不能永远增长下去，遗忘有两种方式。<bookmark mark='a'/>按时间：比保留期更老的整个段会被删除，保留期默认是7天，起始偏移量随之前移。删除一个文件很便宜，这正是要有段的原因之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>按键：压实（compaction）主题只为每个键保留最新的一条记录，位于它原来的偏移量处；而值为空的记录，即墓碑（tombstone），会删除它的键。<bookmark mark='c'/>剩下的就是最新状态，而这就够了：在我们的模拟器里，对50个键的2000次更新压实成50条记录，由它们重建出的表一模一样。

a04eb79a93ac.en: Finally, a partition must survive losing a machine, so it is replicated. <bookmark mark='a'/> One broker leads each partition and takes every write; followers fetch from it as consumers do. A record is committed, and shown to consumers, once every replica in the in-sync set has it; that point is the high watermark. <bookmark mark='b'/> A follower that falls behind is dropped from the set, so one slow disk cannot stall the topic, and the watermark moves on. With acknowledgements from all and at least two in sync, every acknowledged write has two copies. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is Part 39's single-leader replication, not Raft's majority: f plus one replicas survive f failures, and a controller, itself now a Raft log, picks new leaders only from the in-sync set.
a04eb79a93ac.zh: 最后，分区必须经得起失去一台机器，所以它要复制。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个分区由一个 broker 担任领导者，承接所有写入；跟随者像消费者那样从它那里拉取。当同步副本集中的每个副本都拿到一条记录，它就算已提交，并对消费者可见；这个位置就是高水位。<bookmark mark='b'/>落后的跟随者会被移出这个集合，所以一块慢盘拖不住整个主题，高水位照样前进。确认设为 all，并且至少2个副本同步，那么每一次已确认的写入都有两份拷贝。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是第39部分的单主复制，而不是 Raft 的多数派：f 加 1 个副本能经受 f 次故障；而控制器，如今它本身也是一份 Raft 日志，只从同步副本集中挑选新的领导者。

e41d1a07e345.en: Chapter two. Moving a gigabyte a second.
e41d1a07e345.zh: 第二章：每秒搬运一吉字节。

bc80d9be0129.en: Why a gigabyte a second? <bookmark mark='a'/> It is roughly what a ten-gigabit network link carries. In the Kafka paper's experiments a message was two hundred bytes, so a gigabyte a second means five million messages, two hundred nanoseconds each. <bookmark mark='b'/> Set that budget beside Part 34's storage model: one random read from flash costs four hundred budgets, and one from a spinning disk sixty-five thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> So no single message may wait for anything: not a seek, not a round trip, not even a system call of its own. Everything that follows pays for many messages at once.
bc80d9be0129.zh: 为什么是每秒一吉字节？<bookmark mark='a'/>这大约是一条万兆网络链路的承载量。在 Kafka 论文的实验里，一条消息是200字节，所以每秒一吉字节就意味着500万条消息，每条200纳秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这份预算放到第34部分的存储模型旁边：从闪存做一次随机读，要花400份预算；从机械硬盘做一次，要花6万5千份。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以任何一条消息都不能等待任何东西：不能等寻道，不能等一次往返，甚至不能有专属于自己的一次系统调用。接下来的一切，都是一次为许多条消息付账。

ad4927d917fd.en: The first answer is Part 34's rule: write in long runs. <bookmark mark='a'/> A log does nothing else. The producer only appends, and each consumer only reads forward from its offset, so the disk sees long sequential runs, and the kernel's read-ahead fetches pages before anyone asks for them. <bookmark mark='b'/> On Part 34's model disk that is a hundred and fifty megabytes a second, against a third of one. <bookmark mark='c'/> There is no index to maintain either, so an append costs the same with a week of data as with none. And partitions on different disks and brokers add their bandwidth together: seven such disks make a gigabyte a second.
ad4927d917fd.zh: 第一个答案是第34部分的准则：长串地写。<bookmark mark='a'/>日志别的什么都不做。生产者只追加，每个消费者只从自己的偏移量往前读，于是磁盘看到的是长长的顺序访问，内核的预读会在任何人开口之前就把页取来。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第34部分的模型磁盘上，这是每秒150兆字节，而随机访问只有每秒三分之一兆字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>也没有索引要维护，所以有一周的数据时，一次追加的代价和没有数据时一样。而不同磁盘、不同 broker 上的分区，带宽可以相加：7块这样的磁盘，就是每秒一吉字节。

f6009f4563a8.en: The second answer: never send one message alone. <bookmark mark='a'/> The producer collects messages for a partition into a batch and sends the batch in one request. The broker appends it exactly as it arrived, and consumers fetch it the same way. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every request has a fixed overhead, and a batch divides it among all its messages. In the Kafka paper, one producer sent fifty thousand messages a second one at a time, and four hundred thousand in batches of fifty. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is a few milliseconds of latency while a batch fills. And a batch compresses far better than single messages, because neighbouring records repeat each other's fields.
f6009f4563a8.zh: 第二个答案：永远不单独发送一条消息。<bookmark mark='a'/>生产者把发往同一分区的消息收集成一个批次，用一次请求发出整个批次。broker 原样追加它，消费者也以同样的方式取回它。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个请求都有固定的开销，而一个批次把它分摊给其中所有的消息。在 Kafka 论文里，一个生产者逐条发送时每秒发出5万条消息，按每批50条发送时则是40万条。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是批次攒满期间几毫秒的延迟。而且批次比单条消息好压缩得多，因为相邻的记录会重复彼此的字段。

1c2b71255d5e.en: The third answer is to stop touching the bytes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Served the obvious way, data is copied from disk into the kernel's page cache, then into the program's buffer, back into the kernel's socket buffer, and out to the network card: four copies and two system calls, as the Kafka paper counts them. <bookmark mark='b'/> The sendfile call asks the kernel to pass the file's pages straight to a socket, and the middle two copies, and one system call, disappear. <bookmark mark='c'/> This works only because the broker never looks inside a message: the bytes on disk are the bytes the producer sent and the consumer receives. Encrypting in the program, as TLS does, gives zero-copy up.
1c2b71255d5e.zh: 第三个答案，是不再碰这些字节。<bookmark mark='a'/>用显而易见的方式提供数据时，数据要从磁盘复制进内核的页缓存，再进程序的缓冲区，再回到内核的套接字缓冲区，最后送到网卡：按 Kafka 论文的算法，4次复制、2次系统调用。<bookmark mark='b'/>sendfile 调用让内核把文件的页直接交给套接字，中间那两次复制，连同一次系统调用，就都消失了。<bookmark mark='c'/>这之所以可行，只是因为 broker 从不查看消息内部：磁盘上的字节，就是生产者发出的字节，也就是消费者收到的字节。像 TLS 那样在程序里加密，就放弃了零拷贝。

2374f4fece83.en: The last answer is to let the operating system do the caching. <bookmark mark='a'/> Kafka writes every batch to the file system and keeps no cache of its own. The kernel's page cache holds the recent tail, so a consumer that keeps up reads from memory, and the disk is never asked. <bookmark mark='b'/> A consumer replaying yesterday reads from disk, but sequentially. There is no second copy in the program's heap, no garbage collector sweeping millions of messages, and the cache stays warm when the broker restarts. <bookmark mark='c'/> Durability comes from the replicas of chapter one, not from forcing each write to disk. Together, these choices let Jay Kreps report in 2014 two million writes a second on three ordinary machines.
2374f4fece83.zh: 最后一个答案，是让操作系统来做缓存。<bookmark mark='a'/>Kafka 把每个批次写进文件系统，自己不保留任何缓存。内核的页缓存装着最近的尾部，所以跟得上的消费者从内存读取，根本不用去问磁盘。<bookmark mark='b'/>重放昨天数据的消费者要从磁盘读，但是顺序读。程序的堆里没有第二份拷贝，没有垃圾回收器去清扫数百万条消息，而且 broker 重启后缓存依然是热的。<bookmark mark='c'/>持久性来自第一章的副本，而不是强制把每次写入刷到磁盘。这些选择合在一起，让 Jay Kreps 在2014年报告：3台普通机器每秒写入200万条。

1e7c21fa68b8.zh: 第三章：把变更当作事件。

53a18b1fdbc8.en: A company's data lives first in databases, and other systems need copies of it: a search index, a cache, the warehouse. <bookmark mark='a'/> The tempting design is a dual write: the application writes the database, then the index. <bookmark mark='b'/> If it crashes between the two, the database says twelve and the index says ten, for ever, with no error anywhere. <bookmark mark='c'/> Worse, two writers can race, and the two systems apply their writes in opposite orders. <bookmark mark='d'/> The cure is to write once, to the database, and derive every other copy from the one authoritative order: the order in which the database committed.
53a18b1fdbc8.zh: 一家公司的数据首先存放在数据库里，而其他系统需要它的副本：搜索索引、缓存、数据仓库。<bookmark mark='a'/>诱人的设计是双写：应用先写数据库，再写索引。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果它在两次写之间崩溃，数据库说12，索引说10，而且永远如此，任何地方都不报错。<bookmark mark='c'/>更糟的是，两个写入者可能竞争，两个系统以相反的顺序应用它们的写入。<bookmark mark='d'/>解药是只写一次，写进数据库，再从那一个权威的顺序推导出其他所有副本：也就是数据库提交的顺序。

39dd706bc370.en: And the database already writes that order down. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every committed change goes first into its write-ahead log, from Part 35. Change data capture reads that log and publishes each change as an event. <bookmark mark='b'/> An update, an insert and a delete become three events in a topic keyed by the row's id, so each row's changes stay in order, as in chapter one. <bookmark mark='c'/> An event carries the row before and after, and its position in the log. PostgreSQL exposes its log through logical decoding, MySQL through its binary log, and Debezium turns both into streams. <bookmark mark='d'/> To begin, the connector snapshots the table, then follows the log from exactly the position the snapshot saw.
39dd706bc370.zh: 而数据库本来就把这个顺序记了下来。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一次已提交的变更，都先进入它的预写日志，那是第35部分讲的。变更数据捕获（CDC）读取这份日志，把每个变更作为一个事件发布出去。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次更新、一次插入和一次删除，变成一个以行 id 为键的主题里的3个事件，于是每一行的变更都保持顺序，和第一章一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个事件带着该行变更前后的内容，以及它在日志中的位置。PostgreSQL 通过逻辑解码公开它的日志，MySQL 通过它的二进制日志，而 Debezium 把两者都变成流。<bookmark mark='d'/>开始时，连接器先给表做一个快照，然后恰好从快照所看到的那个位置起，跟随日志。

74b4477d8f19.en: Raw change capture has one drawback: it publishes the database's internal tables, and every reader comes to depend on their columns. Part 43's outbox fixes that. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the transaction that marks order forty-two as paid, the service also inserts a row into an outbox table, describing the event. Both commit, or neither does. <bookmark mark='b'/> Change data capture follows only the outbox, and publishes its rows to a topic. <bookmark mark='c'/> The event is a designed contract, order paid, not a copy of a table, and the table can now change shape freely. <bookmark mark='d'/> Delivery is still at least once: a connector that crashes before recording its position publishes again, so readers drop duplicates by the event's identifier.
74b4477d8f19.zh: 原始的变更捕获有一个缺点：它发布的是数据库的内部表，每个读者都会依赖上这些表的列。第43部分的发件箱解决了这个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>在把订单42标记为已付款的那个事务里，服务还会往发件箱表插入一行，描述这个事件。两者要么都提交，要么都不提交。<bookmark mark='b'/>变更数据捕获只跟随发件箱，把其中的行发布到一个主题。<bookmark mark='c'/>事件是一份设计出来的契约，“订单已付款”，而不是某张表的拷贝，于是那张表现在可以自由地改变结构。<bookmark mark='d'/>投递仍然是至少一次：连接器如果在记录自己的位置之前崩溃，就会再发布一遍，所以读者按事件的标识符丢弃重复。

6732d8fb8256.en: Now turn the picture around. If every change is an event, the current state is a summary of the events so far. <bookmark mark='a'/> An account is opened, fifty is deposited, twenty withdrawn, ten deposited, and the balance runs zero, fifty, thirty, forty. <bookmark mark='b'/> The state is a fold: an apply function run over the events, starting from empty. The same events always give the same state. <bookmark mark='c'/> So streams and tables are two views of one thing. Folding a stream of changes gives a table; recording each change to a table gives a stream. Chapter one's compacted topic is exactly this: two thousand updates folded into fifty rows.
6732d8fb8256.zh: 现在把这幅图倒过来看。如果每个变更都是一个事件，那么当前状态就是对迄今为止所有事件的汇总。<bookmark mark='a'/>开一个账户，存入50，取出20，再存入10，余额依次是0、50、30、40。<bookmark mark='b'/>状态是一次折叠：从空开始，在事件上运行一个 apply 函数。同样的事件，总是得到同样的状态。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以流和表是同一样东西的两种视图。折叠一条变更流得到一张表；把一张表的每次变更记录下来，就得到一条流。第一章的压实主题正是如此：2000次更新折叠成50行。

637f5d1489d6.en: Event sourcing, as Martin Fowler described it in 2005, builds a whole application this way. <bookmark mark='a'/> Commands are checked against the current state and, if valid, append events to a log, and that log is the system of record. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each question gets its own read model, a fold over the same events: balances, statements, a search index, fraud features. Separating the write model from the read models is called command query responsibility segregation, or CQRS. A buggy view is rebuilt by replay. <bookmark mark='c'/> The costs: read models lag the log, so users may not see their own writes at once. Events are kept for ever, so their schemas must evolve, as in Part 43, and forgetting a person is hard. And replay grows with history, which snapshots bound.
637f5d1489d6.zh: 事件溯源（event sourcing），正如 Martin Fowler 在2005年描述的，就是用这种方式构建整个应用。<bookmark mark='a'/>命令先对照当前状态检查，如果有效，就往日志里追加事件，而这份日志就是权威记录系统。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一类问题都有自己的读模型，也就是对同一批事件的一次折叠：余额、对账单、搜索索引、反欺诈特征。把写模型和读模型分开，叫作命令查询职责分离，即 CQRS。有缺陷的视图可以通过重放来重建。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是：读模型落后于日志，所以用户可能无法立刻看到自己的写入。事件要永久保留，所以它们的模式必须演进，如第43部分所讲，而且要遗忘一个人很难。重放的代价还随历史增长，这要靠快照来限制。

0f82b5814464.en: Chapter four. Event time and processing time.
0f82b5814464.zh: 第四章：事件时间与处理时间。

6724e1ecd59b.en: Every event in a stream carries two times. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its event time is when it happened, stamped by the phone that recorded the click. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its processing time is when the pipeline sees it, which is always later: a network delay, a queue, or a phone in a tunnel. <bookmark mark='c'/> Plot each event at its event time across and its arrival upwards. Here are 120 simulated events, 2 a second, appearing as the processing clock runs. With no delay they would lie on the diagonal; most land a little above it, the slowest about 18 seconds late. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a pipeline counting one minute's clicks cannot tell from its own clock when that minute's events have all arrived.
6724e1ecd59b.zh: 流中的每个事件都带着两个时间。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的事件时间是它发生的时刻，由记录这次点击的手机打上时间戳。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的处理时间是管道看到它的时刻，总是更晚：一段网络延迟、一个队列，或者一部在隧道里的手机。<bookmark mark='c'/>把每个事件画出来，横轴是事件时间，纵轴是到达时间。这里有120个模拟事件，每秒2个，随着处理时钟走动而出现。如果没有延迟，它们会落在对角线上；大多数落在对角线稍上方，最慢的大约迟到18秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，一条统计某一分钟点击数的管道，无法凭自己的时钟判断那一分钟的事件是否已经全部到达。

27f6201363a1.en: The Dataflow model of Tyler Akidau and his colleagues at Google, in 2015, first asks where in event time a result belongs. <bookmark mark='a'/> Tumbling windows cut time into fixed pieces, here 10 seconds, so every event falls in exactly one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sliding windows have a size and a step, 10 seconds every 5, so each event belongs to two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Session windows are found in the data: one user's run of activity, ended by a gap of 4 seconds, so a late event can merge two sessions into one. <bookmark mark='d'/> All three are defined in event time: the answer depends on what happened, not on when the pipeline heard.
27f6201363a1.zh: Google 的 Tyler Akidau 和同事在2015年提出的 Dataflow 模型，首先问的是：结果在事件时间里属于哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>滚动窗口把时间切成固定的片段，这里是10秒，所以每个事件恰好落在一个窗口里。<bookmark mark='b'/>滑动窗口有大小和步长，这里是每5秒一个10秒的窗口，所以每个事件属于两个窗口。<bookmark mark='c'/>会话窗口是从数据中找出来的：一个用户的一段连续活动，以4秒的空隙结束，所以一个迟到的事件可能把两个会话合并成一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>这三种都是在事件时间里定义的：答案取决于发生了什么，而不是管道何时听说。

9e3cc950276d.en: The second question is when, in processing time, a result can be given. <bookmark mark='a'/> A watermark is the pipeline's running claim that no older event is still on its way. With complete knowledge of the sources it can be exact; usually it is a guess. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ours is the largest event time seen so far, minus 3 seconds, climbing as a staircase behind the events. <bookmark mark='c'/> 11 of the 120 events arrive behind it: they are late. <bookmark mark='d'/> The window of the first ten seconds closes when the watermark passes ten, at about 13 seconds, with 19 of its 20 events. The last arrives 1.7 seconds later, and the answer already given is wrong.
9e3cc950276d.zh: 第二个问题是：在处理时间里，什么时候可以给出结果。<bookmark mark='a'/>水位线（watermark）是管道不断更新的一个断言：不会再有更早的事件还在路上。如果对数据源了如指掌，它可以是精确的；通常它只是一个猜测。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们的水位线是迄今见过的最大事件时间减去3秒，像阶梯一样跟在事件后面爬升。<bookmark mark='c'/>120个事件中有11个到达时落在它后面：它们迟到了。<bookmark mark='d'/>前十秒的窗口在水位线越过10时关闭，大约在第13秒，此时收到了它20个事件中的19个。最后一个事件又晚了1.7秒才到，而已经给出的答案是错的。

57c32866b0b4.en: How long should the watermark wait? We sent 3,000 simulated events through ten-second windows. <bookmark mark='a'/> With no lag, answers come 2 seconds after a window ends, and 530 events are dropped as too late. Waiting five seconds drops 182. <bookmark mark='b'/> Waiting a minute drops just 1, and 29 of the 30 windows are exact, but every answer is more than a minute late. <bookmark mark='c'/> The way out: answer at five seconds, keep each window's state a minute longer, and correct it whenever a late event arrives. Every window ends exact, and first answers come as quickly as before.
57c32866b0b4.zh: 水位线应该等多久？我们让3000个模拟事件通过十秒的窗口。<bookmark mark='a'/>不设滞后时，答案在窗口结束后2秒给出，有530个事件因为太迟而被丢弃。等待5秒，丢弃182个。<bookmark mark='b'/>等待一分钟，只丢弃1个，30个窗口中有29个是精确的，但每个答案都迟了一分钟以上。<bookmark mark='c'/>出路是：在5秒时给出答案，把每个窗口的状态多保留一分钟，每当有迟到事件到达就修正它。每个窗口最终都是精确的，而第一批答案来得和以前一样快。

a3b419b07d36.en: The last two questions are when to emit and how successive answers relate. <bookmark mark='a'/> A trigger decides when a window's result goes out: early, as a speculative answer; on time, when the watermark passes; and late, once for each late event. <bookmark mark='b'/> Accumulation decides what each firing means. Discarding mode emits only what is new. Accumulating mode emits the whole window each time: five, then nine, then ten. With retractions, each firing also withdraws the previous answer, so a consumer summing across windows counts nothing twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our run with a minute of allowed lateness fired 183 refinements. <bookmark mark='d'/> What, where, when and how: the Dataflow model asks these four questions of every pipeline.
a3b419b07d36.zh: 最后两个问题是：何时输出，以及前后相继的答案之间是什么关系。<bookmark mark='a'/>触发器决定窗口的结果何时发出：提前发出，作为推测性的答案；准时发出，在水位线越过时；以及迟到发出，每个迟到事件一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>累积方式决定每次触发意味着什么。丢弃模式只输出新增的部分。累积模式每次输出整个窗口：5，然后9，然后10。带撤回时，每次触发还会撤回上一个答案，所以跨窗口求和的消费者不会把任何东西算两次。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们允许一分钟迟到的那次运行，触发了183次修正。<bookmark mark='d'/>是什么、在哪里、何时、如何：Dataflow 模型对每条管道都问这四个问题。

c676ca8c3b16.zh: 第五章：恰好一次的状态。

5e6b1bb09247.en: A stream processor keeps state: running counts, open windows, the buffers of a join. <bookmark mark='a'/> The state is partitioned by key, like the log it reads, so every key's count lives on exactly one worker, and each event updates it as it passes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then a worker crashes, and its state is gone. The log still holds every event. The question is where to resume. Replay from too late, and events are missed; from too early, and they are counted twice.
5e6b1bb09247.zh: 流处理器保存着状态：运行中的计数、尚未关闭的窗口、连接操作的缓冲区。<bookmark mark='a'/>状态按键分区，就像它所读的日志一样，所以每个键的计数恰好存在一个工作节点上，每个事件经过时都更新它。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后一个工作节点崩溃，它的状态就没了。日志里仍然存着每个事件。问题是从哪里恢复。重放得太晚，事件就被漏掉；太早，它们就被计了两次。

bbe05d4a1faa.en: Paris Carbone and his colleagues gave Apache Flink its answer in 2015, a descendant of Chandy and Lamport's snapshots from Part 38. <bookmark mark='a'/> Records flow from two sources, through two keyed counters, to a sink. <bookmark mark='b'/> To take a checkpoint, each source records its offset and injects a barrier, a marker that travels with the records. <bookmark mark='c'/> A counter with two inputs waits until the barrier has arrived on both, holding back the input that delivered it first, so that its state reflects every event before the barrier and none after. That is alignment. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then it copies its state to storage, in the background, and passes the barrier on. <bookmark mark='e'/> When the sink has every barrier, the checkpoint is complete: offsets and states that describe one consistent cut through the computation. With no cycles and aligned barriers, no records in flight need saving.
bbe05d4a1faa.zh: Paris Carbone 和同事在2015年为 Apache Flink 给出了答案，它是第38部分 Chandy 与 Lamport 快照算法的后裔。<bookmark mark='a'/>记录从两个数据源流出，经过两个按键计数器，流向一个输出端（sink）。<bookmark mark='b'/>要做一个检查点，每个数据源记下自己的偏移量，并注入一个屏障（barrier），这是一个随记录一起传播的标记。<bookmark mark='c'/>有两个输入的计数器要等屏障在两个输入上都到达，同时扣住先送来屏障的那个输入，好让它的状态反映屏障之前的每个事件，而不包括之后的任何事件。这就是对齐。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后它在后台把状态复制到存储中，再把屏障传下去。<bookmark mark='e'/>当输出端收到全部屏障，检查点就完成了：这些偏移量和状态描述了贯穿整个计算的一个一致切面。没有环、屏障又对齐时，不需要保存任何在途记录。

0b695ff262ca.en: We crashed our keyed counter on purpose. <bookmark mark='a'/> 3,032 events, three workers, and checkpoints taken as the stream runs. At offset 1,700, every worker loses its state. <bookmark mark='b'/> Recovery loads the last complete checkpoint, from offset 1,500, and rewinds the source to the same place. 200 events are processed a second time. <bookmark mark='c'/> But they meet the state as it was before they first arrived, and the final counts equal those of a run that never failed. <bookmark mark='d'/> Rewind the source but keep the counts as they stood at the crash, and those 200 events are counted twice: that is at-least-once. <bookmark mark='e'/> Skip the replay, and they are lost: at-most-once. Exactly-once means state and position restored together.
0b695ff262ca.zh: 我们故意让按键计数器崩溃。<bookmark mark='a'/>3032个事件，3个工作节点，流运行期间不断做检查点。在偏移量1700处，每个工作节点都丢失了状态。<bookmark mark='b'/>恢复时载入最后一个完整的检查点，它来自偏移量1500，并把数据源倒回到同一位置。有200个事件被处理了第二次。<bookmark mark='c'/>但它们遇到的状态，是它们第一次到达之前的样子，所以最终计数与一次从未出故障的运行完全相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果倒回数据源，却保留崩溃时的计数，那200个事件就会被计两次：这就是至少一次。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果跳过重放，它们就丢了：这就是至多一次。恰好一次，意味着状态和位置一起恢复。

c031e634e9bb.en: Inside, the state is now exact; outside, some results may have been seen twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> One fix is an idempotent sink. Each result is written as an upsert, keyed by its window and key, so writing the same answer again leaves the table unchanged. <bookmark mark='b'/> The other is a transactional sink. Everything written since the last checkpoint goes into an open transaction that readers cannot see; when the checkpoint completes, it commits. <bookmark mark='c'/> After a crash the open transaction is aborted and its records are written again, so readers see each one once. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is two-phase commit from Part 39, with the checkpoint as coordinator; Kafka gained the transactions it needs in 2017.
c031e634e9bb.zh: 在内部，状态现在是精确的；在外部，有些结果可能已经被看到了两次。<bookmark mark='a'/>一种修正是幂等的输出端。每个结果都以更新插入（upsert）的方式写入，以它的窗口和键为键，所以把同样的答案再写一遍，表不会有任何变化。<bookmark mark='b'/>另一种是事务性的输出端。自上一个检查点以来写出的一切，都进入一个读者看不到的未提交事务；检查点完成时，它就提交。<bookmark mark='c'/>崩溃之后，这个未提交的事务被中止，其中的记录重新写一遍，所以读者对每条记录只看到一次。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是第39部分的两阶段提交，由检查点充当协调者；Kafka 在2017年有了它所需要的事务。

bbad8c11830d.en: So exactly-once is never the property of one component. <bookmark mark='a'/> It needs a source that can be rewound to an offset, which is why logs sit at the front of these pipelines; state checkpointed together with those offsets; and a sink that is idempotent or transactional. <bookmark mark='b'/> Remove any one and the guarantee falls: a source that cannot rewind loses events, and a sink that sends an email sends it twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> Even then, events may be processed more than once; what is exact is their effect. It is the end-to-end argument of Saltzer, Reed and Clark, from Part 36: a guarantee can only be made at the ends.
bbad8c11830d.zh: 所以，恰好一次从来不是某一个组件的性质。<bookmark mark='a'/>它需要一个能倒回到某个偏移量的数据源，这就是日志总是位于这些管道最前端的原因；需要与这些偏移量一起做检查点的状态；还需要一个幂等的或事务性的输出端。<bookmark mark='b'/>去掉任何一个，保证就不成立了：不能倒回的数据源会丢失事件，而发送电子邮件的输出端会把邮件发两次。<bookmark mark='c'/>即便如此，事件仍可能被处理不止一次；精确的是它们的效果。这就是第36部分 Saltzer、Reed 和 Clark 的端到端论证：保证只能在两端做出。

d09bf94c0bde.en: Chapter six. Streaming algorithms in production.
d09bf94c0bde.zh: 第六章：生产中的流式算法。

acbea6a95118.en: The first question asked of a stream is often what is most frequent. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 20's Misra and Gries summary answers it in one pass, here with 99 counters over 4.6 million words. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every count it reports is low, but by at most the number of words divided by 100, about 46 thousand, so the true count lies in the dashed box above each estimate, <bookmark mark='c'/> and any word more frequent than that is certain to be kept. <bookmark mark='d'/> In production what matters is that such summaries merge: each worker summarizes its own partition of each window, and the summaries combine with the same guarantee, as Pankaj Agarwal and his colleagues proved in 2012.
acbea6a95118.zh: 对一条流提出的第一个问题，往往是什么最频繁。<bookmark mark='a'/>第20部分的 Misra 与 Gries 摘要只需一遍就能回答它，这里用99个计数器，处理4.6百万个词。<bookmark mark='b'/>它报告的每个计数都偏低，但至多偏低词的总数除以100，大约46千，所以真实计数落在每个估计值上方的虚线框里，<bookmark mark='c'/>而任何比这更频繁的词都一定会被保留下来。<bookmark mark='d'/>在生产中，要紧的是这类摘要可以合并：每个工作节点为每个窗口里自己的那个分区做摘要，这些摘要合并起来仍有同样的保证，正如 Pankaj Agarwal 和同事在2012年所证明的。

4248488a5672.en: Counting distinct items exactly needs memory for every item. <bookmark mark='a'/> HyperLogLog, from Part 20, keeps only small registers, each holding the longest run of leading zeros among the hashes that land in it. On the corpus's 57,895 distinct words, its error falls from about a quarter with 12 bytes to under one per cent with twelve kilobytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Three kilobytes put the vocabulary within a fifth of a per cent, and count four and a half million distinct five-word phrases as well. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two sketches merge by keeping the larger register in each place, so hourly counts of distinct users roll up into daily ones. <bookmark mark='d'/> Warehouses store such sketches in tables, as BigQuery's HyperLogLog functions do.
4248488a5672.zh: 精确地统计不同元素，需要为每个元素都占用内存。<bookmark mark='a'/>第20部分的 HyperLogLog 只保留一些小寄存器，每个寄存器记录落进它的那些哈希值中最长的一串前导零。在语料的57895个不同的词上，它的误差从用12字节时的大约四分之一，降到用12千字节时的不到百分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>用3千字节，词汇量的误差就在百分之零点二以内，还能同样统计出450万个不同的五词短语。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个草图合并时，在每个位置保留较大的那个寄存器，所以每小时的不同用户数可以汇总成每天的。<bookmark mark='d'/>数据仓库把这样的草图存在表里，BigQuery 的 HyperLogLog 函数就是这样做的。

1776c64dd83d.en: Latency is judged by its median and its ninety-ninth percentile. <bookmark mark='a'/> A KLL sketch, by Zohar Karnin, Kevin Lang and Edo Liberty, keeps levels of samples, each level's items standing for twice as many values as the level below. Over 200,000 simulated latencies, keeping 95 items, its median is close. <bookmark mark='b'/> But at the far tail its ninety-nine point nine percentile is 164 against a true 427: half a per cent wrong in rank, yet more than twice too low in value. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ted Dunning and Otmar Ertl's t-digest attacks the tail directly, with clusters that are large near the median and tiny near the extremes. KLL guarantees rank; t-digest is accurate where latency questions are asked.
1776c64dd83d.zh: 评判延迟，看的是它的中位数和第99百分位数。<bookmark mark='a'/>Zohar Karnin、Kevin Lang 和 Edo Liberty 的 KLL 草图保留若干层样本，每一层的元素所代表的值，是下一层的两倍。在200000个模拟的延迟上，只保留95个元素，它的中位数就很接近。<bookmark mark='b'/>但在远端的尾部，它的第99.9百分位数是164，而真实值是427：按秩只错了百分之零点五，按值却不到真实值的一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>Ted Dunning 和 Otmar Ertl 的 t-digest 直接对付尾部，它的簇在中位数附近很大，在两端极小。KLL 保证的是秩；t-digest 则在延迟问题所关心的地方准确。

da3d3e6305e3.en: Joining two streams is harder than joining two tables, because neither side is ever complete. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here orders and payments are joined on the order number, and a payment counts if it comes within ten minutes of its order. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each order is kept as state while a payment could still arrive. Once the watermark passes ten minutes after it, the order leaves the state, joined, or in an outer join emitted alone. <bookmark mark='c'/> A payment that comes after that finds nothing. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the state is the event rate times the window. A join of a stream with a table, kept current from its change log as in chapter three, holds the table instead.
da3d3e6305e3.zh: 连接两条流比连接两张表更难，因为哪一边都永远不完整。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里订单和付款按订单号连接，一笔付款如果在订单之后10分钟内到来，就算数。<bookmark mark='b'/>只要还可能有付款到达，每个订单就作为状态保存着。一旦水位线越过它之后的10分钟，这个订单就离开状态：或者已经连接上，或者在外连接中被单独输出。<bookmark mark='c'/>在那之后才来的付款，什么也找不到。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以状态的大小是事件速率乘以窗口长度。流与表的连接，表像第三章那样由它的变更日志保持最新，它保存的则是那张表。

76945799e6a7.en: These sketches share the property that matters most in production. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each can be built separately on every partition and every window, and two of them combine into one with the same guarantee: add the counters, keep the larger register, compact the combined samples. <bookmark mark='b'/> So a thousand workers each sketch their share, a tree of merges produces the answer, and the warehouse can store a sketch per hour and roll it up per day or per year. <bookmark mark='c'/> The warehouse is where chapter seven goes next.
76945799e6a7.zh: 这些草图都具有在生产中最要紧的那个性质。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一个都可以在每个分区、每个窗口上分别构建，两个合并成一个后仍有同样的保证：把计数器相加，保留较大的寄存器，压实合并后的样本。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以一千个工作节点各自为自己的那份数据做草图，一棵合并树产生答案，而数据仓库可以每小时存一个草图，再按天或按年汇总。<bookmark mark='c'/>数据仓库，正是第七章接下来要去的地方。

d3b39abdf014.en: First, an argument about architecture. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2011 Nathan Marz proposed what became the Lambda architecture: recompute every answer from the whole log in a batch job, and, because the batch is hours behind, run a stream job alongside for the recent part, merging the two at query time. Every answer is written twice, in two systems that must agree. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2014 Jay Kreps asked why not once. In his Kappa architecture there is only the stream job. To change it, start a second version reading the log from offset zero, let it catch up, and switch the readers over. <bookmark mark='c'/> A batch is just a bounded stream: with event-time windows and replay, as Tyler Akidau argued in 2015, streaming is a superset of batch.
d3b39abdf014.zh: 首先，是一场关于架构的争论。<bookmark mark='a'/>2011年，Nathan Marz 提出了后来被称为 Lambda 架构的方案：用批处理作业从整份日志重新计算每个答案；又因为批处理落后好几个小时，再并行运行一个流作业处理最近的部分，在查询时把两者合并。每个答案都要写两遍，写在两个必须彼此一致的系统里。<bookmark mark='b'/>2014年，Jay Kreps 问：为什么不只写一遍？在他的 Kappa 架构里只有流作业。要修改它，就启动第二个版本，从偏移量0开始读日志，让它追上来，再把读者切换过去。<bookmark mark='c'/>批不过是有界的流：有了事件时间窗口和重放，正如 Tyler Akidau 在2015年所论证的，流处理是批处理的超集。

5596e018c777.en: A warehouse exists because two kinds of question want different machines. <bookmark mark='a'/> An operational database, built for online transaction processing, answers many small requests: fetch order ten forty-two, change its quantity, commit, in milliseconds, touching a few rows found by key. <bookmark mark='b'/> Analysis asks the opposite: total sales by product, over every order ever placed. Edgar Codd named it online analytical processing in 1993. Each query reads a couple of columns of every row, and writes nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> On one database the long scans would starve the short transactions. So the operational system keeps its rows together, in Part 35's B-trees, and a copy of its data, loaded in batches or streamed from its change log, goes to a warehouse built for scans.
5596e018c777.zh: 数据仓库之所以存在，是因为两类问题需要不同的机器。<bookmark mark='a'/>业务数据库为联机事务处理（OLTP）而建，回答大量的小请求：取出1042号订单，修改它的数量，提交，在几毫秒内完成，只碰到按键找到的几行。<bookmark mark='b'/>分析问的恰恰相反：按产品汇总的销售额，覆盖有史以来的每一笔订单。Edgar Codd 在1993年把它命名为联机分析处理（OLAP）。每个查询读取每一行的两三列，什么也不写。<bookmark mark='c'/>放在同一个数据库上，长时间的扫描会让短事务饿死。所以业务系统把每一行的数据存放在一起，放在第35部分的 B 树里；而它的数据的一份副本，或成批载入，或从它的变更日志流过来，送进一个为扫描而建的数据仓库。

dfb4ad0d222e.en: Inside, the design Ralph Kimball set out in 1996 still dominates. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the centre is a fact table: one row per business event, here a sale, holding the numbers you add up, and keys. It is narrow, and billions of rows long. <bookmark mark='b'/> Around it are dimension tables, describing who, what, where and when: the date, the store, the product, the customer. They are wide and full of text, but small. <bookmark mark='c'/> Drawn out, the keys radiate from the centre like a star, which names the schema. Facts are what you measure; dimensions are what you filter and group by.
dfb4ad0d222e.zh: 在仓库内部，Ralph Kimball 在1996年提出的设计至今仍占主导。<bookmark mark='a'/>中心是一张事实表：每个业务事件一行，这里是一笔销售，存放你要加总的数字，以及键。它很窄，却有几十亿行长。<bookmark mark='b'/>围绕它的是维度表，描述谁、什么、哪里、何时：日期、门店、产品、顾客。它们很宽，满是文本，但很小。<bookmark mark='c'/>画出来，键从中心向外辐射，像一颗星，这个模式由此得名：星型模式。事实是你度量的东西；维度是你用来筛选和分组的东西。

2c781c1a81ce.en: A typical question joins the facts to two dimensions: sales by month and category, for one year. <bookmark mark='a'/> The plan almost writes itself. Filter each small dimension and build a hash table from what survives, Part 35's hash join. Then stream the huge fact table past those tables once, keep the rows whose keys hit, and group them. Chapter 11 spreads exactly this over many machines. <bookmark mark='b'/> A snowflake schema normalizes the dimensions further: the product table points to a category table, which points to a department. Less repetition, more joins. <bookmark mark='c'/> But dimensions are small, so the repetition rarely matters, and most warehouses keep the simpler star.
2c781c1a81ce.zh: 一个典型的问题把事实表与两个维度连接：某一年里按月份和类别统计的销售额。<bookmark mark='a'/>计划几乎是自己写出来的。筛选每个小维度，用留下来的行建一张哈希表，这就是第35部分的哈希连接。然后让巨大的事实表从这些哈希表旁边流过一遍，保留键命中的行，再分组。第11章正是把这件事分摊到许多台机器上。<bookmark mark='b'/>雪花模式把维度进一步规范化：产品表指向类别表，类别表再指向部门表。重复更少，连接更多。<bookmark mark='c'/>但维度都很小，重复很少有影响，所以大多数数据仓库保留更简单的星型。

ac5e05e03040.en: Dimensions change, slowly. <bookmark mark='a'/> A customer, Ann, moves from Leeds to York. What should happen to her row? <bookmark mark='b'/> The simplest answer, Kimball's type one, overwrites the city. But then every sale she made in Leeds is now reported as a sale in York, and last year's report changes when it is run again. <bookmark mark='c'/> Type two keeps the history. The old row gets an end date, and a new row, with a new surrogate key, forty-two, begins. Each sale points to the version that was true when it happened. <bookmark mark='d'/> The dimension has become a log of versions, a table that can say what was true on any date, which is where Chapter 10's time travel begins.
ac5e05e03040.zh: 维度会变，只是变得很慢。<bookmark mark='a'/>一位顾客 Ann，从利兹搬到了约克。她的那一行该怎么办？<bookmark mark='b'/>最简单的答案，Kimball 的第一类，直接覆盖城市。但这样一来，她在利兹的每一笔消费，现在都被报告成在约克的销售，而去年的报表再跑一遍，结果就变了。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二类保留历史。旧的那一行得到一个结束日期，新的一行开始，带着新的代理键42。每笔销售都指向它发生时为真的那个版本。<bookmark mark='d'/>维度变成了一份版本的日志，一张能说出任意日期什么为真的表，这正是第10章时间旅行的起点。

34f28803f439.en: A warehouse query reads a few columns of many rows, so store the table by column. <bookmark mark='a'/> A small table of sales. <bookmark mark='b'/> Written row by row, as an operational database stores it, each row's values sit together. <bookmark mark='c'/> Written column by column, each column's values sit together instead. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now ask for the total amount. The row layout reads every byte of every row; the column layout reads one contiguous run, a quarter of the file, read sequentially, as Part 34 showed disks prefer. <bookmark mark='e'/> And one column holds values of a single type, often repeating, which compress far better than a mixed row. C-Store made this argument in 2005.
34f28803f439.zh: 数据仓库的查询读取很多行的少数几列，所以按列来存表。<bookmark mark='a'/>一张小小的销售表。<bookmark mark='b'/>逐行写出，像业务数据库那样存放，每一行的值挨在一起。<bookmark mark='c'/>逐列写出，挨在一起的就变成了每一列的值。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在求总金额。行式布局要读每一行的每一个字节；列式布局只读连续的一段，占文件的四分之一，而且是顺序读取，第34部分说过，磁盘偏爱这种方式。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且一列里的值都是同一种类型，常常重复，比混杂的一行好压缩得多。C-Store 在2005年提出了这个论点。

d28c6f49c06d.en: Parquet, created at Twitter and Cloudera in 2013, is the columnar file most warehouses and data lakes now share. <bookmark mark='a'/> A file begins and ends with four magic bytes, P A R one. In between, rows are cut into row groups, large horizontal slices that can be read in parallel. <bookmark mark='b'/> Within a row group, each column is one contiguous column chunk. <bookmark mark='c'/> A chunk is split into pages, the unit of encoding and compression: often a dictionary page, then data pages, each holding a small header, levels and values. <bookmark mark='d'/> The footer holds the schema and, for every chunk, its place, its encodings and its statistics. A reader fetches the footer first, then seeks to just the chunks it needs.
d28c6f49c06d.zh: Parquet 于2013年诞生于 Twitter 和 Cloudera，如今大多数数据仓库和数据湖共用的就是这种列式文件。<bookmark mark='a'/>文件的开头和结尾都是4个魔数字节：P、A、R、1。在两者之间，行被切成行组，即可以并行读取的大块水平切片。<bookmark mark='b'/>在一个行组里，每一列是一个连续的列块。<bookmark mark='c'/>列块又分成页，页是编码和压缩的单位：通常先是一个字典页，然后是数据页，每页包含一个小页头、级别和值。<bookmark mark='d'/>文件尾存着模式，以及每个列块的位置、编码和统计信息。读取器先取文件尾，再直接定位到它需要的那些列块。

6e0c5775db73.en: Each chunk then picks its encodings. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a column of words, stored plainly, every string in full. <bookmark mark='b'/> Dictionary encoding stores each distinct word once, in a dictionary page, and replaces every value by its small integer index. <bookmark mark='c'/> The indices need only as many bits as the dictionary's size requires, here two, so they are bit-packed: eight values in two bytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> Sorted, equal indices sit together, and Part 21's run-length coding stores each run as a count and a value. <bookmark mark='e'/> And timestamps that creep forward store a first value and then small differences: delta encoding.
6e0c5775db73.zh: 然后每个列块选择自己的编码。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一列词，按原样存储，每个字符串都完整写出。<bookmark mark='b'/>字典编码把每个不同的词在字典页里只存一次，再把每个值替换成它的小整数索引。<bookmark mark='c'/>索引所需的位数只取决于字典的大小，这里是两位，所以把它们按位打包：8个值占2个字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>排序之后，相等的索引挨在一起，第21部分的游程编码把每一段存成一个计数和一个值。<bookmark mark='e'/>而缓慢递增的时间戳，存下第一个值，再存一串小的差值：这就是增量编码。

ceebf708324d.en: What do these save on real text? <bookmark mark='a'/> We took three hundred thousand words of the novels as one column. Plainly, with their lengths, it takes two point five eight megabytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> There are thirty thousand five hundred and fifteen distinct words, so indices need fifteen bits; with the dictionary page they come to zero point nine three megabytes, about a third. Gzip alone does a little better, zero point eight. <bookmark mark='c'/> In reading order a word almost never repeats eight times running, so run lengths add nothing. Sort the column, and they halve it, to zero point four seven, under a fifth of plain. <bookmark mark='d'/> A hundred thousand timestamps shrink from eight hundred kilobytes to a hundred and thirty-eight, eleven bits each. And both are undone by simple arithmetic, far cheaper to decode than gzip.
ceebf708324d.zh: 这些编码在真实文本上能省多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们取小说中的30万个词作为一列。按原样存储，连同它们的长度，要占2.58兆字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>不同的词有30515个，所以索引需要15位；加上字典页，一共0.93兆字节，大约三分之一。单用 gzip 稍好一点，0.8。<bookmark mark='c'/>按阅读顺序，一个词几乎从不连续重复8次，所以游程编码毫无帮助。把这一列排序，游程编码就能让它减半，降到0.47，不到原样的五分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>10万个时间戳从800千字节缩小到138千字节，每个11位。而且两者都只需简单的算术就能还原，解码比 gzip 便宜得多。

123efd2bea2d.en: Statistics give the largest saving of all: not reading. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are a million rows in ten row groups, and a query that wants x between four hundred and twenty thousand and four hundred and thirty thousand. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the table is sorted by x, each group's minimum and maximum are close together, and only one group overlaps the filter. The other nine are skipped unopened: the filter has been pushed down into the scan. <bookmark mark='c'/> In random order, every group spans nearly everything, and all ten must be read. <bookmark mark='d'/> So statistics pay only when data is sorted or clustered by the columns people filter on, which is why table layout matters so much.
123efd2bea2d.zh: 统计信息带来最大的节省：根本不读。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有100万行，分成10个行组，还有一个查询，要找 x 在42万到43万之间的行。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果表按 x 排序，每个行组的最小值和最大值离得很近，只有一个行组与过滤条件重叠。另外9个连打开都不用就被跳过：过滤条件已经被下推到了扫描里。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果是随机顺序，每个行组几乎都跨越整个范围，10个都必须读。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，只有当数据按人们用来过滤的列排序或聚集时，统计信息才有回报，这就是表的布局如此重要的原因。

59f89af4edc8.en: Chapter nine. Nested data in columns.
59f89af4edc8.zh: 第九章：列中的嵌套数据。

9373115237e1.en: Real data is rarely flat: logs and documents are records nested inside records. Dremel, Google's interactive query engine, described by Sergey Melnik and colleagues in 2010, stored them in columns anyway. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are three books, with repeated chapters, each with repeated keywords. One chapter has no keywords; one book has no chapters. <bookmark mark='b'/> The schema says which fields are required and which repeat. <bookmark mark='c'/> Take one column, chapters dot keywords, and write out its values: sea, whale, inn, Highbury. The structure is gone. Which keywords shared a chapter, or a book? And the empty chapter and the empty book have vanished. Two small numbers beside each value bring it all back.
9373115237e1.zh: 真实的数据很少是扁平的：日志和文档都是嵌套在记录里的记录。Dremel 是 Google 的交互式查询引擎，由 Sergey Melnik 和同事在2010年描述，它照样把这些记录存进了列里。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有三本书，有重复的章节，每章又有重复的关键词。有一章没有关键词；有一本书没有章节。<bookmark mark='b'/>模式说明哪些字段是必需的，哪些会重复。<bookmark mark='c'/>取一列，chapters 点 keywords，写出它的值：sea、whale、inn、Highbury。结构不见了。哪些关键词同属一章，或者同属一本书？而且那个空的章节和那本空的书都消失了。每个值旁边的两个小数字，能把这一切都找回来。

c7de14db705a.en: The first number is the repetition level. <bookmark mark='a'/> For each value, in order, it says at which repeated field along the path this value repeats. Zero means a new record has begun. One means a new chapter, in the same book. Two means another keyword, in the same chapter. <bookmark mark='b'/> Walk the column. Sea starts the first book: zero. Whale follows it in the same chapter: two. Inn starts a new chapter: one. <bookmark mark='c'/> The empty chapter still needs a slot, a null with level one, and so does the book with no chapters, a null with level zero. Highbury starts a new book: zero. The path has two repeated fields, so the levels run from zero to two.
c7de14db705a.zh: 第一个数字是重复级别。<bookmark mark='a'/>对每个值，它依次说明这个值是在路径上的哪个重复字段处重复。0表示开始了一条新记录。1表示同一本书里的一个新章节。2表示同一章里的又一个关键词。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿着这一列走一遍。sea 开始第一本书：0。whale 跟在它后面，在同一章里：2。inn 开始一个新章节：1。<bookmark mark='c'/>空的章节仍然需要一个位置，一个级别为1的空值；没有章节的那本书也一样，一个级别为0的空值。Highbury 开始一本新书：0。这条路径上有两个重复字段，所以级别从0到2。

facfdf1243ab.en: The second number, the definition level, says how much of the path exists. <bookmark mark='a'/> Count the fields along chapters dot keywords, optional or repeated, that are really present. <bookmark mark='b'/> A real keyword has its chapter and itself: two, the maximum. <bookmark mark='c'/> The empty chapter exists but holds no keyword: one. The book without chapters has neither: zero. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a null is never stored as a value, only as a level below the maximum, which says exactly where the missing part begins. A column of required fields needs no definition levels, and one outside any repeated field no repetition levels, so flat tables pay nothing.
facfdf1243ab.zh: 第二个数字是定义级别，它说明路径中有多少部分存在。<bookmark mark='a'/>沿着 chapters 点 keywords，数一数那些可选的或重复的字段中，真正存在的有几个。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个真实的关键词，有它的章节，也有它自己：2，即最大值。<bookmark mark='c'/>空的章节存在，但没有关键词：1。没有章节的书两者都没有：0。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以空值从不作为一个值存储，只表现为一个低于最大值的级别，它准确地说明缺失的部分从哪里开始。由必需字段组成的列不需要定义级别，不在任何重复字段之内的列不需要重复级别，所以扁平的表什么代价也不用付。

b0e53a1c3469.en: A reader rebuilds the records from the levels alone, without ever seeing the tree. <bookmark mark='a'/> Read the pairs in order. A repetition level of zero starts a new record. A definition level of zero means that record has no chapters, and we move on. Otherwise, a repetition level of one or less opens a new chapter, and a definition level of two appends a keyword to it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Six pairs later the three books are back, exactly: two keywords and then one in the first two chapters, an empty third chapter, an empty book, and Highbury. <bookmark mark='c'/> And because every column carries its own levels, a query can rebuild just the parts of the records it reads, and never touch the rest.
b0e53a1c3469.zh: 读取器只凭这些级别就能重建记录，根本不用看到那棵树。<bookmark mark='a'/>按顺序读这些数对。重复级别为0，就开始一条新记录。定义级别为0，表示这条记录没有章节，我们继续往下。否则，重复级别小于等于1就开一个新章节，定义级别为2就往里追加一个关键词。<bookmark mark='b'/>读完六个数对，三本书就原样回来了：前两章分别有两个和一个关键词，第三章是空的，一本空书，还有 Highbury。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且因为每一列都带着自己的级别，查询可以只重建它读取的那部分记录，其余部分完全不碰。

84159e15daf0.en: Why is this worth the trouble? <bookmark mark='a'/> The levels are tiny integers, two bits each here, bit-packed and run-length coded like any other column; in regular data they are nearly constant, and almost free. A missing value costs only its levels. In return, nested records get every benefit of columns: a query about keywords reads keywords and their levels, and nothing else. <bookmark mark='b'/> Dremel's paper reported aggregations over trillion-row tables in seconds, and the system became the engine behind Google's BigQuery. <bookmark mark='c'/> Parquet adopted the same levels, in every data page. In memory, Apache Arrow stores the same trees another way, as offsets into child arrays with bitmaps that mark the nulls.
84159e15daf0.zh: 为什么值得这么麻烦？<bookmark mark='a'/>级别是很小的整数，这里每个两位，像其他任何列一样按位打包、做游程编码；在规整的数据里它们几乎是常数，几乎不占空间。一个缺失的值只花费它的级别。作为回报，嵌套的记录获得了列存储的全部好处：关于关键词的查询只读关键词和它们的级别，别的什么都不读。<bookmark mark='b'/>Dremel 的论文报告说，在万亿行的表上做聚合只需几秒，这个系统后来成了 Google BigQuery 背后的引擎。<bookmark mark='c'/>Parquet 采用了同样的级别，存在每一个数据页里。在内存中，Apache Arrow 用另一种方式存放同样的树：用指向子数组的偏移量，加上标记空值的位图。

d00330e974db.en: Chapter ten. Tables on object storage.
d00330e974db.zh: 第十章：对象存储上的表。

97dcb33914dd.en: A data lake is a folder of chapter eight's files in object storage. Is that a table? <bookmark mark='a'/> A job writes its output as three files. <bookmark mark='b'/> A reader that lists the folder halfway through sees two, and silently computes half an answer. <bookmark mark='c'/> A crashed job leaves its files behind, and overwriting means deleting, then writing. Part 45's object store makes each object atomic, but nothing spans two. And listing a million files takes a thousand requests, one after another.
97dcb33914dd.zh: 数据湖就是对象存储里的一个文件夹，装着第八章的那些文件。这算是一张表吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>一个作业把它的输出写成三个文件。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个读者在写到一半时列出文件夹，看到的是两个，于是不声不响地算出了半个答案。<bookmark mark='c'/>崩溃的作业会把它的文件留在那里，而覆盖意味着先删除、再写入。第45部分的对象存储让每个对象都是原子的，但没有任何东西能跨越两个对象。而且列出一百万个文件需要一千次请求，一次接一次。

ae4171e451e6.en: Apache Iceberg, begun at Netflix, and Delta Lake, from Databricks, give the same answer: keep the list of files in files. <bookmark mark='a'/> In Iceberg a table is a tree: data files; manifests listing them; a manifest list for each snapshot; and a metadata file with the schema and history. A commit writes new files, bottom up, and changes none. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then it swaps one pointer in a catalog, from the old metadata file to the new. That one atomic step is the commit: readers see all of it or none. <bookmark mark='c'/> The new snapshot reuses the old manifest, so a commit costs a few small files. <bookmark mark='d'/> Manifests also record column ranges, so planners prune files without listing anything.
ae4171e451e6.zh: 始于 Netflix 的 Apache Iceberg 和来自 Databricks 的 Delta Lake 给出了同样的答案：把文件清单也存在文件里。<bookmark mark='a'/>在 Iceberg 中，一张表是一棵树：数据文件；列出它们的清单文件（manifest）；每个快照一个清单列表；以及一个存放模式和历史的元数据文件。一次提交自底向上写出新文件，不改动任何已有文件。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后它在目录服务（catalog）里切换一个指针，从旧的元数据文件指向新的。这一个原子步骤就是提交：读者要么看到全部，要么什么也看不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>新快照复用旧的清单文件，所以一次提交只需几个小文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>清单文件还记录各列的取值范围，所以查询规划器不用列出任何东西就能剪掉文件。

5a7d45ff35b8.en: Delta Lake keeps the same information as a log. <bookmark mark='a'/> A folder beside the data holds numbered commits, each listing files added and removed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Replayed in order, they give the table: two files, then a third, then the first two compacted into one, then another. The table is a fold over its log, chapter three's event sourcing, kept in the object store itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every ten commits a Parquet checkpoint records the folded state, so readers replay only what follows. <bookmark mark='d'/> And committing means creating the next number only if nobody has: a conditional write, which S3 has offered since 2024.
5a7d45ff35b8.zh: Delta Lake 把同样的信息存成一份日志。<bookmark mark='a'/>数据旁边的一个文件夹里存着编了号的提交，每个提交列出新增和删除的文件。<bookmark mark='b'/>按顺序重放，就得到这张表：两个文件，然后第三个，然后前两个被压实成一个，然后又一个。表是对它的日志的一次折叠，也就是第三章的事件溯源，只不过就存在对象存储本身里。<bookmark mark='c'/>每10次提交，一个 Parquet 检查点记录下折叠后的状态，所以读者只需重放其后的部分。<bookmark mark='d'/>而提交意味着创建下一个编号，前提是还没有人创建过：这是一次条件写入，S3 从2024年起提供了这种功能。

797e81a59589.en: Two jobs commit to the same table at once. <bookmark mark='a'/> Both read version forty-one and work without locks, checking only at commit: Kung and Robinson's optimistic control, from Part 35. <bookmark mark='b'/> Job A finishes first and creates version forty-two. Job B tries forty-two as well, and fails: the name is taken. <bookmark mark='c'/> B reads what A committed. If A touched nothing B read or rewrote, as when both only append, B retries as forty-three, writing just a new log entry. <bookmark mark='d'/> If A rewrote files that B read, B's work is stale and must be redone.
797e81a59589.zh: 两个作业同时向同一张表提交。<bookmark mark='a'/>两者都读取了版本41，不加锁地工作，只在提交时检查：这就是第35部分 Kung 和 Robinson 的乐观并发控制。<bookmark mark='b'/>作业 A 先完成，创建了版本42。作业 B 也尝试42，失败了：这个名字已被占用。<bookmark mark='c'/>B 读取 A 提交的内容。如果 A 没有碰过 B 读过或重写的任何东西，比如两者都只是追加，B 就以43重试，只写一条新的日志项。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果 A 重写了 B 读过的文件，B 的工作就过时了，必须重做。

d7e05899c116.en: How much does contention cost? <bookmark mark='a'/> Our instrument simulates writers committing fifty times each, after a random amount of work, one unit on average. <bookmark mark='b'/> When every commit conflicts, losers redo their work. At sixteen writers each commit is retried almost four times, and sixteen writers manage under three times the rate of one. <bookmark mark='c'/> When writers only append, losers merely renumber, and sixteen commit eleven times as fast as one. So let concurrent writers append, or touch different partitions.
d7e05899c116.zh: 争用的代价有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的仪器模拟一些写入者，每个提交50次，每次提交前做随机长度的工作，平均一个单位。<bookmark mark='b'/>当每次提交都冲突时，失败者要重做它们的工作。16个写入者时，每次提交要重试将近4次，而16个写入者的提交速率还不到1个写入者的3倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>当写入者只追加时，失败者只需重新编号，16个写入者的提交速度是1个的11倍。所以，让并发的写入者只做追加，或者去碰不同的分区。

9fa3e1af22e2.en: Because commits never change old files, every old version is still there. <bookmark mark='a'/> In Spark SQL, either format can be read as of a version or a timestamp, starting from an older snapshot. <bookmark mark='b'/> A bad write is undone by restoring an earlier version, itself a new commit. Audits can ask what a report saw last March, and models can retrain on the data they first saw. <bookmark mark='c'/> A vacuum later deletes the files that no recent snapshot needs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Armbrust and colleagues named the result in 2021: a lakehouse, a warehouse's guarantees over open files on cheap storage.
9fa3e1af22e2.zh: 因为提交从不改动旧文件，每个旧版本都还在。<bookmark mark='a'/>在 Spark SQL 中，两种格式都可以按某个版本或某个时间戳来读取，从一个较早的快照开始。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次错误的写入，可以通过恢复到更早的版本来撤销，而恢复本身又是一次新的提交。审计可以问一份报表在去年三月看到的是什么，模型可以用它们最初见到的数据重新训练。<bookmark mark='c'/>之后，一次清理（vacuum）会删除近期任何快照都不再需要的文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>Armbrust 和同事在2021年给这个结果起了名字：湖仓（lakehouse），在廉价存储上的开放文件之上，提供数据仓库的保证。

b7fa93923e60.en: Chapter eleven. Queries on a thousand machines.
b7fa93923e60.zh: 第十一章：千台机器上的查询。

0321b3214be2.en: A warehouse query is too big for one machine, so it runs on many. <bookmark mark='a'/> The table's files are spread over the workers, and the coordinator cuts the plan into fragments that every worker runs on its own share. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each worker first counts its own rows per store, a partial aggregate, and so sends three numbers instead of its rows. <bookmark mark='c'/> An exchange operator then hashes each store to one worker, which adds up that store's partial counts: Part 39's MapReduce shuffle, inside a query. <bookmark mark='d'/> The coordinator gathers the answers. DeWitt's Gamma machine had this shape in 1986; Redshift, BigQuery, Snowflake and Trino have it today.
0321b3214be2.zh: 数据仓库的查询对一台机器来说太大了，所以它要在许多台机器上运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>表的文件分散在各个工作节点上，协调节点把执行计划切成若干片段，每个工作节点都在自己的那一份数据上运行这些片段。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个工作节点先按门店统计自己的行数，这是一次部分聚合，于是它发送的是三个数字，而不是它的那些行。<bookmark mark='c'/>接着，一个交换（exchange）算子把每个门店哈希到一个工作节点，由它把这个门店的部分计数加起来：这就是第39部分 MapReduce 的洗牌，只不过发生在一个查询内部。<bookmark mark='d'/>协调节点收集答案。DeWitt 的 Gamma 机器在1986年就是这个形状；今天的 Redshift、BigQuery、Snowflake 和 Trino 也是。

462049209d8c.en: Joins are where the network bill comes from: a big table, B, meets a small one, S, on N workers. <bookmark mark='a'/> A broadcast join sends a whole copy of S to every worker. B never moves; each worker joins its share of B against the copy, with Part 35's hash join. The cost is S rows, N times over. <bookmark mark='b'/> A shuffle hash join repartitions both tables by the join key, so matching rows meet on one worker. A row stays put only if it already sits on the right worker, one time in N, so the cost is B plus S, times one minus one over N.
462049209d8c.zh: 网络账单来自连接（join）：一张大表 B，在 N 个工作节点上与一张小表 S 相连接。<bookmark mark='a'/>广播连接把 S 的一整份副本发给每个工作节点。B 从不移动；每个工作节点用第35部分的哈希连接，把自己那一份 B 与这份副本连接起来。代价是 S 的行数，乘以 N。<bookmark mark='b'/>洗牌哈希连接按连接键把两张表都重新分区，让匹配的行在同一个工作节点上相遇。只有当一行本来就位于正确的工作节点上时，它才留在原地，这种情况是 N 次里有1次，所以代价是 B 加 S，再乘以1减 N 分之一。

24b469a41c50.en: Which is cheaper? <bookmark mark='a'/> In our cost model B has a billion rows of a hundred bytes, there are a hundred workers, and S grows from ten thousand rows to a hundred million. <bookmark mark='b'/> Broadcasting grows tenfold with S. Shuffling costs about a hundred gigabytes whatever S is, because B dominates. <bookmark mark='c'/> Set the costs equal: broadcast wins while S is below about B over N, here ten million rows, one percent of B. <bookmark mark='d'/> Optimizers choose from estimated sizes, and cautiously, since every worker must hold the copy in memory: Spark broadcasts only tables it estimates under ten megabytes, by default. A wrong estimate, Part 35's guessing of sizes, makes either choice a disaster.
24b469a41c50.zh: 哪个更便宜？<bookmark mark='a'/>在我们的代价模型里，B 有10亿行，每行100字节，有100个工作节点，S 从1万行增长到1亿行。<bookmark mark='b'/>广播的代价随 S 成十倍地增长。洗牌无论 S 多大，都要花大约100吉字节，因为 B 占了大头。<bookmark mark='c'/>令两种代价相等：只要 S 小于大约 B 除以 N，广播就更划算，这里是1000万行，即 B 的百分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>优化器根据估计的大小来选择，而且很谨慎，因为每个工作节点都必须把副本放在内存里：Spark 默认只广播它估计小于10兆字节的表。一个错误的估计，也就是第35部分对大小的猜测，会让任何一种选择都变成灾难。

eea40d6d4dea.en: Hashing spreads keys evenly, not rows. <bookmark mark='a'/> If one key is hot, all its rows go to one worker. <bookmark mark='b'/> We measured it: two hundred thousand rows on sixteen workers, one key holding a fifth. The busiest worker gets almost four times its fair share, and a query finishes only when its slowest worker does. Part 39's backup tasks cannot help: that worker is not slow, its share is large. <bookmark mark='c'/> The fix is salting: split the hot key into eight random sub-keys, and copy its matches on the small side eight times. The slowest worker now carries 1.2 times the ideal. <bookmark mark='d'/> Chapter 6's heavy-hitter sketches find hot keys cheaply, and Spark's adaptive execution splits skewed partitions as the query runs.
eea40d6d4dea.zh: 哈希让键均匀分布，而不是让行均匀分布。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果某个键很热，它的所有行都会去往同一个工作节点。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们测了一下：16个工作节点上有20万行，其中一个键占了五分之一。最忙的工作节点分到的几乎是它应得份额的4倍，而一个查询只有在最慢的工作节点完成时才算完成。第39部分的备份任务帮不上忙：那个工作节点并不慢，只是它的那一份太大了。<bookmark mark='c'/>解决办法是加盐（salting）：把热键拆成8个随机的子键，并把小表一侧与它匹配的行复制8份。现在，最慢的工作节点承担的是理想值的1.2倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>第六章的高频项（heavy hitter）草图能廉价地找出热键，而 Spark 的自适应执行会在查询运行时拆分倾斜的分区。

ea00a63e3206.en: Inside each worker, how operators pass data matters as much as the network. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 35's iterator model, Volcano's, passes one row per call: a function call and a branch for every row and every operator. <bookmark mark='b'/> Vectorized execution, from MonetDB X100 in 2005, passes a batch: about a thousand values of each column, two thousand and forty-eight in DuckDB. <bookmark mark='c'/> A filter runs one tight loop over the price column and writes a selection vector, the positions that passed; the sum reads only those positions of the amount column. <bookmark mark='d'/> Loops without calls become Part 24's SIMD instructions, often on chapter eight's dictionary codes. The other answer, HyPer's, compiles each query to machine code.
ea00a63e3206.zh: 在每个工作节点内部，算子之间如何传递数据，和网络同样重要。<bookmark mark='a'/>第35部分的迭代器模型，也就是 Volcano 的模型，每次调用传递一行：每一行、每一个算子，都要一次函数调用和一次分支。<bookmark mark='b'/>向量化执行来自2005年的 MonetDB X100，它传递的是一批数据：每一列大约一千个值，在 DuckDB 里是2048个。<bookmark mark='c'/>过滤器在价格列上跑一个紧凑的循环，写出一个选择向量，也就是通过过滤的那些位置；求和只读取金额列中这些位置上的值。<bookmark mark='d'/>没有函数调用的循环会变成第24部分的 SIMD 指令，而且常常作用在第八章的字典编码上。另一种答案来自 HyPer：把每个查询编译成机器码。

8e74b892710c.en: Chapter twelve. Data you can trust.
8e74b892710c.zh: 第十二章：值得信赖的数据。

b2886caa9330.en: The first threat to a pipeline is its input changing shape. <bookmark mark='a'/> An order record gains a currency field; last year's records lack it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Backward compatibility asks whether new readers can read old data: yes, because the new field has a default, which the reader fills in. Forward compatibility asks whether old readers can read new data: yes again; they skip fields they do not know. <bookmark mark='c'/> Avro's rules settle every change. A field without a default breaks backward compatibility, widening an integer breaks forward, and a rename breaks both. <bookmark mark='d'/> A schema registry checks each new version against its topic's rule, backward by default, before producers use it. And Iceberg names columns by number, so renames are safe there: Part 43's API evolution, for data.
b2886caa9330.zh: 对一条管道的第一个威胁，是它的输入改变了形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>订单记录多了一个货币字段；去年的记录没有它。<bookmark mark='b'/>向后兼容问的是：新的读者能否读取旧数据？能，因为新字段有默认值，由读者填上。向前兼容问的是：旧的读者能否读取新数据？同样能；它们会跳过自己不认识的字段。<bookmark mark='c'/>Avro 的规则对每一种改动都有定论。没有默认值的字段会破坏向后兼容，把整数加宽会破坏向前兼容，而重命名两者都会破坏。<bookmark mark='d'/>模式注册表（schema registry）会在生产者使用每个新版本之前，按其主题的规则检查它，默认是向后兼容。而 Iceberg 用编号来指代列，所以在那里重命名是安全的：这就是第43部分的 API 演进，用在了数据上。

3c2b8fe44fe9.en: Most pipelines begin in a database that another team owns. <bookmark mark='a'/> The orders service writes its tables and publishes changes, through chapter three's outbox, to a topic. <bookmark mark='b'/> A data contract makes that interface explicit, like an API: fields and types, meanings, such as amount in pence including tax, freshness, ownership, and which changes are allowed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Consumers build on the contract, never on the service's internal tables. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now a developer renames amount to total. The contract is checked in the producer's continuous integration, so the change fails there, before deployment, not in a dashboard three days later. A breaking change needs a new version, run beside the old.
3c2b8fe44fe9.zh: 大多数管道都起始于另一个团队拥有的数据库。<bookmark mark='a'/>订单服务写入它的表，并通过第三章的发件箱，把变更发布到一个主题。<bookmark mark='b'/>数据契约让这个接口变得明确，就像 API 一样：字段和类型；含义，比如金额以便士为单位、含税；新鲜度；归属；以及允许哪些改动。<bookmark mark='c'/>消费者在契约之上构建，从不依赖这个服务的内部表。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在，一位开发者把 amount 改名为 total。契约在生产者的持续集成中接受检查，所以这次改动在那里、在部署之前就失败了，而不是三天后才在某个仪表盘上暴露出来。破坏性的改动需要一个新版本，与旧版本并行运行。

4b30c5928aec.en: Contracts say what data should be; tests check what it is. <bookmark mark='a'/> In dbt, which builds warehouse tables from SQL, tests sit beside each table: this key is unique and never empty, this status takes only these values, every customer exists in the customers table. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each test compiles to a query for the rows that break it, and passes when the query returns nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> Run such tests on chapter thirteen's stream of novels. Uniqueness finds two books sent twice. Reconciling word totals with the source catches the pipeline without deduplication, nearly seven percent high, and the early watermark, ten percent low. <bookmark mark='d'/> Volume and freshness checks catch the failures nobody wrote a rule for.
4b30c5928aec.zh: 契约说的是数据应该是什么样；测试检查的是它实际是什么样。<bookmark mark='a'/>dbt 用 SQL 构建数据仓库的表，在 dbt 里，测试就放在每张表旁边：这个键唯一，而且从不为空；这个状态只取这几个值；每个客户都存在于客户表中。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个测试都会编译成一个查询，找出违反它的行；查询什么都没返回，测试就通过。<bookmark mark='c'/>在第十三章的小说流上运行这样的测试。唯一性测试找出了被发送两次的两本书。把单词总数与数据源对账，能抓出不去重的管道，它高了将近百分之七；也能抓出过早的水位线，它低了百分之十。<bookmark mark='d'/>数据量和新鲜度检查，能抓住那些没人为之写过规则的故障。

59292dc747a1.en: Tables are built from tables, and their dependencies form a graph. <bookmark mark='a'/> Sources feed staging tables, which feed the marts analysts query, which feed dashboards, models and reports. dbt reads this graph from the references in each model's SQL and builds it in topological order: Part 41's build system, with tables for files. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now a test on the staging payments table fails. Following edges forward, the graph names everything now suspect; those builds stop, and their owners are told. <bookmark mark='c'/> Following edges backward leads towards the cause, the payments interface. <bookmark mark='d'/> Column-level lineage narrows it further, and the OpenLineage standard lets engines report these edges as they run.
59292dc747a1.zh: 表由表构建而成，它们的依赖构成一张图。<bookmark mark='a'/>数据源供给暂存表，暂存表供给分析师查询的数据集市，数据集市再供给仪表盘、模型和报表。dbt 从每个模型的 SQL 里的引用读出这张图，并按拓扑顺序构建：这就是第41部分的构建系统，只是用表代替了文件。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在，暂存的支付表上有一个测试失败了。沿着边向前走，这张图会列出现在所有可疑的东西；这些构建会停下来，它们的负责人会收到通知。<bookmark mark='c'/>沿着边向后走，就会走向原因：支付接口。<bookmark mark='d'/>列级血缘能把范围进一步缩小，而 OpenLineage 标准让引擎在运行时报告这些边。

2e321c8f1909.en: Tests help most before anyone reads the data. <bookmark mark='a'/> Chapter ten's tables make that cheap: a job writes its new snapshot but does not publish it, and readers still see version forty-one. <bookmark mark='b'/> The tests run on the staged snapshot. If they pass, publishing is one atomic pointer swap, and every reader moves to forty-two at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> If they fail, the snapshot is never published, and readers keep the last good version. This is write, audit, publish, which Iceberg supports with branches of a table. <bookmark mark='d'/> Trust, then, is engineered: contracts where data is made, tests at every step, lineage to trace failures, and atomic publishing.
2e321c8f1909.zh: 测试在任何人读取数据之前最有用。<bookmark mark='a'/>第十章的表让这件事变得廉价：一个作业写出它的新快照，但不发布它，读者看到的仍是版本41。<bookmark mark='b'/>测试在这个暂存的快照上运行。如果通过，发布就是一次原子的指针交换，每个读者同时切换到版本42。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果失败，这个快照永远不会被发布，读者继续使用上一个好的版本。这就是写入、审计、发布（write, audit, publish），Iceberg 用表的分支来支持它。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，信任是工程造出来的：在数据产生的地方有契约，每一步都有测试，有血缘来追踪故障，还有原子的发布。

835d10ad3618.en: Chapter thirteen. The Job as a stream.
835d10ad3618.zh: 第十三章：作为流的那项任务。

856859b8acf2.en: The Job, one last time in a new shape. <bookmark mark='a'/> The thirty novels arrive as a stream, one event per book, each carrying its words and its place in a publishing schedule as its event time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Most arrive a second or two after they are due. Three arrive twenty seconds late, as if from a phone that was offline. <bookmark mark='c'/> And two are sent twice, by a producer that retried. The task is a top twenty that is correct at every moment, and in the end equal to the batch answer of every earlier part.
856859b8acf2.zh: 那项任务，最后一次，换一个新的形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>30部小说以流的形式到达，每本书一个事件，每个事件携带它的词，以及它在出版时间表中的位置，作为它的事件时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>大多数书在应到时间之后一两秒到达。有3本迟到了20秒，就像来自一部曾经离线的手机。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有2本被发送了两次，因为生产者重试了。要做的是一个前20名，它在每一刻都正确，并且最终与前面每一部分的批处理答案相同。

159744b2b2a6.en: We ran three pipelines over the same stream. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first deduplicates by book and keeps its counts as state: it counts 4,498,120 words, and its top twenty is identical to the batch answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second does not deduplicate. The two books sent twice are counted twice, 4,797,994 words, and the counts are wrong. <bookmark mark='c'/> The third uses a watermark that waits five seconds and drops anything later, so the three late books are missing: 4,048,309 words. <bookmark mark='d'/> The state of a stream is a fold over its events, applied once per key and checkpointed with the source's offset. And because this top twenty is over all time, it needs no watermark at all; a windowed answer would face chapter four's choice between waiting and being wrong.
159744b2b2a6.zh: 我们在同一条流上运行了三条管道。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一条按书去重，并把计数保存为状态：它数出4498120个词，它的前20名与批处理答案完全一致。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二条不去重。被发送两次的两本书被数了两次，得到4797994个词，计数是错的。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三条使用一个等待5秒的水位线，并丢弃更晚到达的一切，所以那3本迟到的书不见了：4048309个词。<bookmark mark='d'/>流的状态是对其事件的一次折叠，对每个键只应用一次，并与数据源的偏移量一起做检查点。而且因为这个前20名是针对全部时间的，它根本不需要水位线；如果是按窗口的答案，就要面对第四章那个选择：要么等待，要么出错。

0b728d82ecc3.en: The ledger gets row seventeen. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Job as a stream on one machine: about 4 seconds for all thirty books, deduplicated and exact. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is slower than the best batch rows, because it does the bookkeeping a stream needs. What it buys is an answer that is current after every book, rather than after the last one.
0b728d82ecc3.zh: 账本添上第17行。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一台机器上作为流的那项任务：处理全部30本书大约要4秒，已去重，结果精确。<bookmark mark='b'/>它比最好的那几行批处理要慢，因为它做了一条流所需要的记账工作。它换来的是一个每处理完一本书就是最新的答案，而不是等到最后一本之后才有。

b95617a0de3f.en: Chapter fourteen, the frontier. Can every query be kept up to date, cheaply?
b95617a0de3f.zh: 第十四章：前沿。每个查询都能被廉价地保持最新吗？

1d5649a223ea.en: Streams and tables are converging. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a query over a table, joins, filters, counts, and ask that its answer stay current as rows arrive. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rather than rerun it, push each change through the plan as a delta: one new order becomes one joined row, which passes the filter or not, and changes one count by one. That is incremental view maintenance, and its promise is work in proportion to the change, not the data. <bookmark mark='c'/> Differential dataflow, from Frank McSherry and colleagues in 2013, extended it to iterative and recursive computations, and DBSP, by Mihai Budiu and colleagues in 2023, gave an algebra that makes any streaming query incremental. <bookmark mark='d'/> Which queries can be maintained cheaply, and with how much state, is open; for some joins, provably, they cannot.
1d5649a223ea.zh: 流和表正在趋于融合。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个针对表的查询，有连接、过滤、计数，并要求它的答案随着行的到达始终保持最新。<bookmark mark='b'/>不是重新运行它，而是把每个变更作为一个增量（delta）推过执行计划：一条新订单变成一条连接后的行，它要么通过过滤，要么不通过，并让某一个计数改变1。这就是增量视图维护，它的承诺是工作量与变更成正比，而不是与数据成正比。<bookmark mark='c'/>Frank McSherry 和同事在2013年提出的差分数据流（differential dataflow），把它推广到了迭代和递归的计算；Mihai Budiu 和同事在2023年提出的 DBSP，给出了一套代数，能让任何流式查询变成增量的。<bookmark mark='d'/>哪些查询能被廉价地维护、需要多少状态，仍是未解决的问题；对于某些连接，可以证明，做不到。

26ed30e543fd.en: How small can a summary of a stream be? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a KLL sketch of two hundred thousand latencies. Keeping 95 of them, it puts the median within about one percent of the true rank; keeping 1,326, within a few hundredths of a percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> KLL, by Zohar Karnin, Kevin Lang and Edo Liberty in 2016, is optimal up to constant factors: no summary can do much better in the worst case. <bookmark mark='c'/> Lower bounds like this, starting with Noga Alon, Yossi Matias and Mario Szegedy in 1996, tell a designer what is impossible before anything is built. <bookmark mark='d'/> Open questions remain at the tails, where relative accuracy matters most, for sketches that can be merged and kept private, and for summaries that answer joins.
26ed30e543fd.zh: 一条流的摘要能有多小？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是对20万个延迟值做的一个 KLL 草图。保留其中95个，它给出的中位数与真实排名相差约百分之一以内；保留1326个，就在百分之零点零几以内。<bookmark mark='b'/>KLL 由 Zohar Karnin、Kevin Lang 和 Edo Liberty 在2016年提出，它在常数因子以内是最优的：在最坏情况下，没有任何摘要能做得好很多。<bookmark mark='c'/>像这样的下界，从1996年 Noga Alon、Yossi Matias 和 Mario Szegedy 的工作开始，在任何东西建成之前，就告诉设计者什么是不可能的。<bookmark mark='d'/>未解决的问题仍然存在：在尾部，那里相对精度最要紧；在既能合并、又能保护隐私的草图上；以及在能回答连接的摘要上。

504df2a81b18.en: The deepest limit is time. <bookmark mark='a'/> A watermark is a guess that no older events will arrive, and every choice of how long to wait trades completeness for latency: from four fifths of the events within two seconds to all but one of them after a minute. <bookmark mark='b'/> Answering early and then correcting escapes the trade: a five-second watermark with a minute of allowed lateness fired 183 refinements and ended with every window exact. The price is state, and consumers that must accept corrections. <bookmark mark='c'/> Watermarks with guarantees, derived from measured delays, and a semantics of streaming SQL that every engine agrees on, are open problems.
504df2a81b18.zh: 最深的极限是时间。<bookmark mark='a'/>水位线是一个猜测：猜不会再有更早的事件到达，而每一种等待多久的选择，都是在完整性和延迟之间做权衡：从两秒内得到五分之四的事件，到一分钟后只差一个事件。<bookmark mark='b'/>先早早回答，再加以修正，就能摆脱这种权衡：一个5秒的水位线，加上允许一分钟的迟到，触发了183次修正，最终每个窗口都是精确的。代价是状态，以及必须接受修正的消费者。<bookmark mark='c'/>有保证的水位线，从测得的延迟推导出来；以及一套所有引擎都认同的流式 SQL 语义：这些都是未解决的问题。

5783a0e76bc0.en: Open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Which queries can be maintained incrementally, in time proportional to each change, and with how much state. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watermarks with guarantees, derived from measured delays rather than guessed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Small summaries that answer joins and group-bys with bounded error. <bookmark mark='d'/> And layouts learned from the workload: which sort order, partitioning and encoding a table should have. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem asks which windowed stream joins can be maintained exactly using space that grows more slowly than the window itself.
5783a0e76bc0.zh: 未解决的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>哪些查询能被增量地维护，时间与每次变更成正比，又需要多少状态。<bookmark mark='b'/>有保证的水位线，从测得的延迟推导出来，而不是靠猜。<bookmark mark='c'/>小的摘要，能以有界的误差回答连接和分组（group-by）。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有从工作负载中学习出来的布局：一张表应该采用哪种排序顺序、分区方式和编码。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题问的是：哪些按窗口的流连接能被精确地维护，而所用空间的增长比窗口本身更慢。

293fe9e4474d.en: What we built in this part. A partitioned log, where order holds per key and consumer groups share the partitions, and a compacted log that rebuilds the same state from fifty records instead of two thousand. State as a fold over events. Windows over event time, and watermarks that trade completeness for latency, unless an answer may be corrected later. Barrier snapshots that let a computation crash and recover with exactly-once state. Columnar files, whose dictionaries and run lengths make a column of words a fraction of its size, and Dremel's two levels that put nested records into flat columns. One idea runs through it: record what happened, in order, once, and every answer can be derived, and derived again.
293fe9e4474d.zh: 这一部分我们构建了什么。一个分区日志，其中顺序按键保持，消费者组分担各个分区；还有一个压实后的日志，它用50条记录而不是2000条，重建出同样的状态。作为事件折叠的状态。基于事件时间的窗口，以及在完整性和延迟之间做权衡的水位线，除非答案允许事后修正。屏障快照，让一次计算可以崩溃，再以恰好一次的状态恢复。列式文件，它的字典和游程让一列词只占原来大小的一小部分；还有 Dremel 的两种级别，把嵌套记录放进扁平的列。一个思想贯穿其中：按顺序、只记录一次发生了什么，那么每个答案都能被推导出来，并且能再推导一次。

12755fb49da8.en: Where this comes back. Part 47 builds a search index from a log of documents and keeps it current. Parts 48 and 49 design feeds, timelines and analytics systems from these pieces. Part 50 turns logs, metrics and traces on the running system itself. Part 57 asks what can be learned from data at this scale, and Part 55 what it takes to trust the pipeline that delivered it.
12755fb49da8.zh: 这些内容会在哪里再出现。第47部分从一个文档日志构建搜索索引，并让它保持最新。第48和49部分用这些部件设计信息流、时间线和分析系统。第50部分把日志、指标和追踪用在运行中的系统本身。第57部分会问，在这种规模的数据上能学到什么；第55部分则问，要信任交付这些数据的管道，需要做到什么。

dfab1be90b68.en: In practice. Key a log by whatever must stay in order, give it enough partitions for the future, and compact the logs that hold state. Window streams by event time, choose their lateness on purpose, and write results to sinks that tolerate repeats. Capture changes from the database's log or an outbox, never by writing twice. Store tables as columnar files, sorted or clustered by the filter people use most. And broadcast the small side of a join, and look for hot keys before they find you.
dfab1be90b68.zh: 实践中。用必须保持顺序的那个东西作为日志的键，为未来留出足够的分区，并压实那些保存状态的日志。按事件时间给流开窗，有意识地选择它们的迟到容许，并把结果写入能容忍重复的输出端。从数据库的日志或发件箱捕获变更，绝不靠写两次。把表存成列式文件，按人们最常用的过滤条件排序或聚簇。还有，广播连接中较小的一侧，并在热键找上你之前先找到它们。

18077666425b.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: give our stream processor sliding windows and allowed lateness, and measure how much state it has to keep. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: which joins over windows of a stream can be maintained exactly with less memory than the window itself.
18077666425b.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是构建题：给我们的流处理器加上滑动窗口和允许迟到，并测量它需要保存多少状态。最后一道标有星号，是研究题：在一条流的窗口上，哪些连接能被精确地维护，而所用内存比窗口本身更少。

e957b18b67ad.en: Next time, Part 47: search engines. How do you find the ten most relevant pages among billions in a fifth of a second? An inverted index turns search into merging sorted lists, compression keeps them in memory, a probabilistic model of relevance gives BM25, and a random surfer gives PageRank.
e957b18b67ad.zh: 下一次，第47部分：搜索引擎。如何在五分之一秒内，从几十亿个网页中找出最相关的十个？倒排索引把搜索变成合并有序列表，压缩让它们留在内存里，一个关于相关性的概率模型给出 BM25，而一个随机冲浪者给出 PageRank。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
